title: Bespoke Carpentry & Joinery
content: Bespoke carpentry is fundamentally about understanding how timber behaves within the unique context of an individual building. In period and character properties across Wiltshire, from timber-framed cottages to classical stone residences, no two rooms share identical lines. Walls undulate, ceiling joists dip, and floors settle naturally over decades and centuries. True architectural joinery does not attempt to force standardized dimensions onto these spaces. Instead, it begins with careful measurement and a deep appreciation for the building's historical integrity, producing timberwork that looks and feels as though it has always belonged. At our workshop at Bradfield Farm in Hullavington, raw timber is machined and jointed using traditional bench methods, including wedged mortise and tenon joints, housing joints, and clean rebates that provide structural permanence. Whether crafting bespoke wall panelling, replacing damaged historical mouldings, fitting substantial oak lintels, or building custom timber screens, every component is tailored to the exact architectural narrative of your home. The transition from workshop to site is handled with equal care. On-site fitting requires patient scribing to marry timber seamlessly to out-of-plumb stone or uneven lime plaster without relying on modern mastic or unsightly cover strips. We work with carefully sourced native and European hardwoods, alongside stable, durable timbers such as Accoya for exposed elements, ensuring that every piece balances aesthetic warmth with seasonal stability. We believe in letting clean lines, balanced proportions, and the honest texture of wood speak for themselves. By focusing entirely on bespoke work rather than mass production, we ensure your property receives thoughtful, durable woodwork built to the highest possible trade standards.

title: Bespoke Kitchens
content: A kitchen in a period or character home should never feel like a series of modular boxes simply screwed to a wall. Older properties present distinct architectural conditions, including historic flagstone floors, low ceiling bressummers, exposed stone reveals, and chimney breasts that require a bespoke, considered approach to cabinetry. We design, craft, and fit kitchens that respond directly to the proportions and vernacular of the room, creating an environment that balances timeless joinery with effortless modern practicality. Every cabinet is constructed using traditional in-frame techniques, where doors and drawers are individually fitted flush within a solid timber face frame. Carcases are made from robust, high-grade materials, while drawers are built with solid hardwood sides, classic dovetail joints, and concealed soft-close runners that offer tactile weight and longevity. Storage is planned around how you cook and live, incorporating custom larder units, bespoke spice racks, integrated bin systems, and tailored island workstations. We offer a choice of finishes, from hand-painted cabinetry using heritage palettes to natural oiled timbers like character oak and walnut that showcase organic grain patterns. Coordinating smoothly with other trades, such as plumbers, electricians, and stone templaters, is an integral part of our process. Because everything is manufactured in our Hullavington workshop, we maintain total control over quality, tolerances, and design details from the initial sketch to the final adjustment on site. The result is a bespoke kitchen that respects the character of your home, withstands the daily rigours of family life, and ages with quiet dignity over decades of use.

title: Fitted Furniture
content: Historic and character homes are rich in personality, but they rarely offer straightforward, symmetrical spaces for standard off-the-shelf furniture. Chimney breasts create awkward, uneven alcoves, attic bedrooms feature sloping ceiling eaves, and older hallways frequently hide neglected recesses beneath staircases. Our bespoke fitted furniture is designed to unlock the full potential of these challenging spaces, transforming architectural idiosyncrasies into beautiful, highly functional storage that complements the fabric of the room. Rather than utilizing generic modular systems with awkward infill panels, every piece is built from scratch to the precise contours of your walls and ceilings. We design and build floor-to-ceiling wardrobes, bespoke library bookcases, media cabinetry, study desks, and integrated boot room storage complete with panelled benches and cubbies. The exterior can be styled to mirror original architectural features, incorporating matching skirting boards, custom architraves, delicate beading, and raised-and-fielded or flat-panel doors. Internally, the storage is customized to your exact requirements, with tailored combinations of adjustable shelving, solid dovetail drawer boxes, internal lighting runs, and hanging rails. We work in both natural hardwoods and durable moisture-resistant timbers designed for fine hand-painted or sprayed finishes. Every component is prepared at our workshop near Chippenham and then meticulously scribed into place on site, ensuring seamless integration against lath-and-plaster walls, stone reveals, and historic floorboards. This thoughtful approach ensures your home gains purposeful storage that looks integral to the original architecture rather than added as an afterthought.

title: Bespoke Timber Doors
content: A door is the most tactile architectural element in any home. The solid weight in the hand, the smooth swing of the hinges, and the satisfying engagement of a latch provide an immediate impression of quality and craftsmanship. In older Wiltshire properties, doorways are seldom standard modern sizes; settling foundations, thick stone reveals, and handcrafted historic frames mean that off-the-shelf doors rarely fit or look appropriate. We design and manufacture bespoke internal and external timber doors tailored precisely to non-standard structural openings and authentic period proportions. For country cottages and rustic conversions, we handcraft traditional ledged and braced doors using hand-selected European oak, featuring traditional through-tenons, decorative chamfers, and bespoke bead profiles. For Georgian, Victorian, and Edwardian homes, we produce authentic panelled doors, ranging from four-panel configurations to intricate six-panel entrance designs with raised-and-fielded timber panels and bolection mouldings. Exterior doors are constructed from exceptionally stable, weather-resistant timbers, including engineered hardwoods and Accoya, designed to resist seasonal movement, swelling, and sticking during wet winters. We integrate discrete modern draught-sealing systems, high-security multi-point or traditional five-lever mortise locks, and heritage glazing options without compromising the delicate historic sightlines of the door. From the proportion of the top rail to the depth of the bottom kick rail, every detail is considered, resulting in bespoke doors that preserve the acoustic privacy, thermal comfort, and historic elegance of your home.

title: Sash & Casement Windows
content: Windows define the face and soul of a period property. In historic market towns and conservation villages throughout Wiltshire and the Cotswolds, getting the details right is not just a matter of aesthetics; it is vital for complying with listed building requirements and conservation area regulations. Modern factory-made units with thick glazing bars and flat plastic profiles strip character away from older homes. We craft bespoke timber sliding sash and flush casement windows that faithfully replicate historical sightlines while offering outstanding thermal performance and weather resistance. Our traditional box sash windows are constructed using time-tested methods, incorporating weighted pulley mechanisms with lead counterweights, waxed cotton cords, and traditional meeting rails. For casement windows, we build flush-fitting frames hung on authentic butt hinges, secured with traditional stay pins and fasteners. We work extensively with Accoya and durable hardwoods, ensuring our window frames remain dimensionally stable and will not bind, rattle, or twist when the seasons change. Depending on the listing status and conservation requirements of your property, we offer a range of glazing options, including authentic single glazing with traditional linseed putty finishes, or ultra-slim heritage double glazing that avoids the thick, distorted reflections of modern units while dramatically improving insulation. Every window is handcrafted in our Hullavington workshop to the exact dimensions of your existing stone or timber reveals, restoring weather tightness, acoustic comfort, and period authenticity to your property.

title: Staircases & Joinery
content: The staircase is frequently the architectural centerpiece of a property, anchoring the entrance hall and setting the tone for the entire interior. Designing and building a staircase for a period home requires a rigorous balance between spatial geometry, structural stability, and statutory building regulations. In character properties and historic cottages, stairwells are often compact and awkward, demanding bespoke configurations like tight winding kites, quarter landings, or space-saving curved flights that fit within restricted structural openings without sacrificing headroom or ease of ascent. We design, manufacture, and install custom timber staircases, working in a range of styles from classical cut-string stairs with decorative bracketed tread ends to understated closed-string designs suited to modest cottages. Every element is crafted with care: solid hardwood treads and risers are deeply housed, glued, and wedged into solid strings to prevent creaks and settlement over time. We produce a wide range of balustrade components, including continuous swept handrails, elegant volutes, bespoke turned newel posts, and delicate square or turned spindles that reflect the architectural period of the building. Whether replacing a failing flight, opening up a neglected hallway, or designing access for an attic conversion, we oversee the entire process from structural calculations and workshop fabrication through to careful on-site installation. We ensure that your staircase not only meets all current safety standards, but also provides an enduring, beautifully crafted piece of joinery that elevates the character of your home.
